title: Equality of Two Path Encodings
statement: A binary word encodes a reachable directed graph instance using the matrix encoding if and only if it encodes one using the raw-list encoding. In the matrix encoding, a word has the form obtained by pairing the unary vertex count, the row-by-row adjacency bits, and the binary representations of the start and target vertices, with both vertices in range and the target reachable from the start. In the raw-list encoding, the adjacency list has exactly $n^2$ bits, both vertices are less than $n$, the word is formed from the unary count, that list, and the two vertex representations, and the target is reachable using edges whose corresponding list entries are true.
